title: Eight Kinds of Word
welcome_lead: Every word has a job. Meet all eight.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on the eight word classes.

walkthroughs.body_html: The eight word classes: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, determiner.
A noun names ('Sara'). A pronoun stands in ('she'). They keep writing from repeating names.
Adjectives describe nouns ('a swift fox'). Adverbs describe verbs ('ran swiftly'). Many adverbs end in -ly.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between transitive and intransitive verbs?
options: Transitive verbs end in -ed and intransitive in -ing.
Transitive verbs are action verbs and intransitive are linking verbs.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
Transitive verbs take a direct object ('she ate the cake'); intransitive verbs don't ('she slept'). Some verbs are both depending on use ('she ran' / 'she ran the company').

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.

Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
Alternating between languages or varieties within a conversation or even a single utterance — often patterned by context, topic, identity or audience. Code-switching is rule-governed, not random.
Code-switching shows the speaker doesn't know either language properly.
